Bloom's contribution to the Firefighter Community Fund will support families facing food insecurity across Oxford and Lafayette County

SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE) continued its season-long partnership with ESPN Radio's College Football Campus Tour this week in Oxford, Mississippi, ahead of Saturday's Georgia-Ole Miss matchup.

Ahead of the game, Bloom visited Oxford Fire Department Station 1 at 399 McElroy Drive and presented a $10,000 donation to the Firefighter Community Fund, a nonprofit established by members of the Oxford Fire Department to support local families facing food insecurity.

The Firefighter Community Fund works with Oxford Love Packs and Commodores Care to provide financial assistance and essential goods to children and families across Oxford and Lafayette County. The organization also provides Thanksgiving meals to families in need, with its work funded through community donations and events including the annual 9/11 Memorial Stair Climb.

“The strongest communities are built by people who look out for one another, often in ways most of us never see,” said Natalie Sunderland, Chief Marketing Officer at Bloom Energy. “Oxford’s firefighters do more than respond when their neighbors need help. Through the Firefighter Community Fund, they are addressing needs in their community long before an emergency call comes in. We are proud to support that commitment and the families it reaches across Oxford and Lafayette County.”

“Our firefighters see firsthand the needs families in our community face, and being there for our community is at the heart of what we do,” said Josh Ferguson, Director of the Firefighter Community Fund. “We’re grateful for Bloom Energy’s support, which will help us reach and feed more local families at a time of year when coming together and looking out for our neighbors means so much.”

The Oxford visit is part of Bloom's season-long partnership with ESPN Radio's College Football Campus Tour, which is bringing Bloom to college communities across the country and using each stop to recognize the firefighters and first responders who help keep those communities safe.

Bloom will also be on campus Saturday ahead of the Georgia-Ole Miss game as ESPN Radio's College Football Campus Tour powered by Bloom Energy brings its live broadcast and interactive Fan Zone to Oxford.

Bloom Energy empowers enterprises to meet soaring energy demands and responsibly take charge of their power needs. The company’s fuel cell systems provide ultra-reliable, clean and highly scalable onsite electricity for Fortune 500 customers around the world, including data centers, semiconductor manufacturing, large utilities and other commercial and industrial sectors, as well as mission-critical organizations in local communities, such as hospitals, college campuses and retailers. MILLBROOK, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 6, 2026 / Global Self Storage, Inc. (NASDAQ:SELF), a real estate investment trust that owns, operates, manages, acquires, and redevelops self-storage properties, reported results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. All comparisons are to the same year-ago period unless otherwise noted.

Q3 2026 Highlights

  • Total revenues increased 0.6% to $3.2 million.
  • Net income decreased 16.0% to $417,000 or $0.04 per diluted share.
  • Same-store revenues increased 0.6% to $3.2 million.
  • Same-store cost of operations increased 2.5% to $1.3 million.
  • Same-store net operating income (NOI) decreased 0.6% to $2.0 million (see definition of this and other non-GAAP measures and their reconciliation to GAAP, below).
  • Same-store occupancy as of September 30, 2026 was 92.9%, compared to 93.2% as of September 30, 2025.
  • Same-store average tenant duration of stay as of September 30, 2026 was a record level of approximately 3.7 years, and increased compared to approximately 3.5 years as of September 30, 2025.
  • Funds from operations (FFO), a non-GAAP measure, increased 5.8% to $1.1 million or $0.09 per diluted share.
  • Adjusted FFO (AFFO), a non-GAAP measure, increased 4.7% to $1.1 million or $0.10 per diluted share.
  • Maintained and covered quarterly dividend of $0.0725 per common share.
  • Capital resources as of September 30, 2026 totaled approximately $24.3 million, comprised of $7.5 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash; $2.3 million in marketable securities; and $14.5 million available under the company's revolving credit facility.

First Nine Months 2026 Highlights

  • Total revenues increased 0.9% to $9.6 million.
  • Net income increased 0.4% to $1.7 million or $0.15 per diluted share from $1.7 million or $0.15 per diluted share.
  • Same-store revenues increased 0.9% to $9.6 million.
  • Same-store cost of operations increased 6.8% to $3.9 million.
  • Same-store NOI decreased 2.8% to $5.7 million.
  • FFO decreased 5.9% to $2.9 million or $0.26 per diluted share.
  • AFFO decreased 5.1% to $3.2 million or $0.28 per diluted share.
  • Maintained and covered dividends totaling $0.2175 per common share.

Dividend

On September 1, 2026, the company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.0725 per share, consistent with the quarterly dividend for the year-ago period and previous quarter. The quarterly distribution represents an annualized dividend rate of $0.29 per share.

Company Objective

The objective of Global Self Storage is to increase value over time for the benefit of its stockholders. Toward this end, the company will continue to execute its strategic business plan, which includes funding acquisitions, either directly or through joint ventures, and expansion projects at its existing properties. The company's board of directors regularly reviews the strategic business plan, with emphasis on capital formation, debt versus equity ratios, dividend policy, use of capital and debt, FFO and AFFO performance, and optimal cash levels.

The management of Global Self Storage believes that the company's continued operational performance and capital resources position it well to continue executing its strategic business plan.

Management Commentary

"In Q3, we delivered positive same-store revenue growth, a record-level average tenant duration of stay of approximately 3.7 years at quarter-end, and strong growth in FFO and AFFO," said CEO and president of Global Self Storage, Mark C. Winmill. "During the quarter, our competitor move-in rate metrics analysis kept our rates competitive, while our proprietary revenue rate management program increased existing tenant rates and optimized store occupancy.

"Our digital marketing initiatives also supported maintaining strong occupancy by highlighting our outstanding customer reviews, including a record-level average rating above 4.9 out of 5 stars at quarter-end.

"Our customer service efforts-providing a clean, safe and convenient rental process-continued to attract high-quality, long-term tenants. These efforts also strengthened local brand loyalty and drove strong referral and word-of-mouth demand for our storage units and services.

"This quarter, we neared completion of the replacement of our kiosks with a QR code-based quick access page for unit rentals. This followed our transition from a live agent call center to an AI-based virtual agent call center in the second quarter. With these changes in place, we currently expect marketing expenses to decrease for the remainder of 2026.

"At our Lima, Ohio property, our second-largest property, we converted certain student housing space into approximately 2,400 leasable square feet of all-climate-controlled units in Q1 2026. Total area occupancy following the conversion was approximately 90.6%. The property reached approximately 94.1% occupancy as of September 30, 2026.

"While our focus on cost control helped reduce G&A expenses by 5.5% during the quarter, store operating expenses increased primarily due to higher employment costs and real estate property taxes. We currently expect growth in store-level employment costs related to headcount to return to lower historic levels, partially offset by inflationary increases in compensation rates and additional compensation costs as we potentially add stores. We also expect inflationary increases in administrative costs for the remainder of 2026. We continue to appeal property tax reassessments as they arise, but there is no guarantee that assessments will be reduced.

"With approximately $24.3 million in capital resources, we believe we can continue to execute our strategic business plan through acquisitions, directly or through joint ventures, and expansion projects at existing properties. We continue to review store and portfolio acquisition opportunities and may pursue additional third-party management relationships through Global MaxManagement, seeking to broaden our revenue base and pipeline of potential acquisitions.

"Looking ahead, we currently expect rental income growth to come from continued existing tenant rent increases, higher move-in rental rates, lower promotional discounts and higher occupancy. We anticipate existing tenant rent increases for the remainder of 2026 to be similar to those in the prior year. With our disciplined operating approach, loyal tenant base and capital resources, we believe we are well positioned to pursue growth opportunities and build long-term value for our stockholders."

Q3 2026 Financial Summary

Total revenues increased 0.6% to $3.2 million in the third quarter of 2026. The increase was primarily attributable to increases in existing tenant rates under its proprietary revenue rate management program.

Total operating expenses decreased 1.2% to $2.47 million compared to $2.50 million in the same year-ago period. The decrease was primarily attributable to lower general and administrative expenses, partially offset by higher store operating expenses.

Operating income increased 6.7% to $777,000, compared to $728,000 in the same period last year. The increase was the result of the operating effects noted above.

Net income totaled $417,000 or $0.04 per diluted share compared to $496,000 or $0.04 per diluted share in the same year-ago period.

Capital resources as of September 30, 2026 totaled approximately $24.3 million, comprised of $7.5 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash and $2.3 million in marketable securities, with $14.5 million available under the company's revolving credit facility.

Q3 2026 Same-Store Results

As of September 30, 2026, the company owned 12 same-store properties and managed a single third-party-owned property. There were no non-same-store properties.

For the third quarter of 2026, same-store revenues increased 0.6% to $3.2 million compared to the same period last year.

Same-store cost of operations increased 2.5% to $1.3 million compared to $1.2 million in the same period last year. The increase was primarily due to increased expenses for employment costs and real estate property taxes, partially offset by lower marketing expenses.

Same-store NOI decreased 0.6% to $1.96 million compared to $1.97 million in the same period last year. The decrease was primarily due to an increase in store operating expenses.

Same-store occupancy was 92.9% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 93.2% as of September 30, 2025.

Same-store average tenant duration of stay as of September 30, 2026 reached a record level of approximately 3.7 years, compared to approximately 3.5 years as of September 30, 2025.

Q3 2026 Operating Results

Net income in the third quarter of 2026 was $417,000 or $0.04 per diluted share compared to $496,000 or $0.04 per diluted share in the third quarter of 2025.

Property operations expenses increased to $1.3 million from $1.2 million in the same period last year.

General and administrative expenses decreased 5.5% to $780,000 from $826,000 in the same year-ago period. The decrease was primarily attributable to lower professional fees.

Interest expense decreased to $200,000 from $209,000 in the same year-ago period.

FFO increased 5.8% to $1.1 million or $0.09 per diluted share compared to FFO of $1.0 million or $0.09 per diluted share in the same period last year.

AFFO increased 4.7% to $1.15 million or $0.10 per diluted share compared to AFFO of $1.10 million or $0.10 per diluted share in the same period last year.

First Nine Months 2026 Financial Summary

Total revenues increased 0.9% to $9.6 million in the first nine months of 2026. The increase was primarily attributable to increases in existing tenant rates under the company's proprietary revenue rate management program.

Total operating expenses increased 4.5% to $7.6 million compared to $7.3 million in the same year-ago period. The increase was primarily attributable to higher store operating expenses and general and administrative expenses.

Operating income decreased 10.4% to $2.0 million, compared to $2.3 million in the same period last year. The decrease was the result of the operating effects noted above.

Net income totaled $1.7 million or $0.15 per diluted share compared to $1.7 million or $0.15 per diluted share in the same year-ago period.

First Nine Months 2026 Same-Store Results

For the first nine months of 2026, same-store revenues increased 0.9% to $9.6 million compared to $9.5 million in the same period last year. The increase was due primarily to higher existing tenant rates under the company's proprietary revenue rate management program.

Same-store cost of operations increased 6.8% to $3.9 million compared to $3.6 million in the same period last year. The increase was primarily due to increased expenses for employment costs and real estate property taxes, partially offset by lower marketing expenses.

Same-store NOI decreased 2.8% to $5.7 million compared to $5.9 million in the same period last year. The decrease was primarily due to an increase in store operating expenses.

First Nine Months 2026 Operating Results

Net income in the first nine months of 2026 was $1.7 million or $0.15 per diluted share compared to $1.7 million or $0.15 per diluted share in the first nine months of 2025.

Property operations expenses increased to $3.9 million from $3.6 million in the same period last year.

General and administrative expenses increased to $2.5 million from $2.4 million in the same year-ago period. The increase was primarily attributable to higher employment costs.

Interest expense decreased to $607,000 from $647,000 in the same year-ago period.

FFO decreased 5.9% to $2.9 million or $0.26 per diluted share compared to FFO of $3.1 million or $0.27 per diluted share in the same period last year.

AFFO decreased 5.1% to $3.2 million or $0.28 per diluted share compared to AFFO of $3.3 million or $0.30 per diluted share in the same period last year.

About Global Self Storage

Global Self Storage is a self-administered and self-managed REIT that owns, operates, manages, acquires, and redevelops self-storage properties. The company's self-storage properties are designed to offer affordable, easily accessible and secure storage space for residential and commercial customers. Through its wholly owned subsidiaries, the company owns and/or manages 13 self-storage properties in Connecticut, Illinois, Indiana, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, and Oklahoma.

For more information, go to ir.globalselfstorage.us or visit the company's customer site at www.globalselfstorage.us. You can also follow Global Self Storage on X, LinkedIn and Facebook.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures

Funds from operations ("FFO") and FFO per share are non-GAAP measures defined by the National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts ("NAREIT") and are considered helpful measures of REIT performance by REITs and many REIT analysts. NAREIT defines FFO as a REIT's net income, excluding gains or losses from sales of property, and adding back real estate depreciation and amortization. The Company also excludes changes in unrealized gains or losses on marketable equity securities. FFO and FFO per share are not a substitute for net income or earnings per share. FFO is not a substitute for GAAP net cash flow in evaluating our liquidity or ability to pay dividends, because it excludes financing activities presented on our statements of cash flows. In addition, other REITs may compute these measures differently, so comparisons among REITs may not be helpful. However, the Company believes that to further understand the performance of its stores, FFO should be considered along with the net income and cash flows reported in accordance with GAAP and as presented in the Company's financial statements.

Adjusted FFO ("AFFO") and AFFO per share are non-GAAP measures that represent FFO and FFO per share excluding the effects of stock-based compensation, business development, capital raising, and acquisition related costs and non-recurring items, which we believe are not indicative of the Company's operating results. AFFO and AFFO per share are not a substitute for net income or earnings per share. AFFO is not a substitute for GAAP net cash flow in evaluating our liquidity or ability to pay dividends, because it excludes financing activities presented on our statements of cash flows. We present AFFO because we believe it is a helpful measure in understanding our results of operations insofar as we believe that the items noted above that are included in FFO, but excluded from AFFO, are not indicative of our ongoing operating results. We also believe that the analyst community considers our AFFO (or similar measures using different terminology) when evaluating us. Because other REITs or real estate companies may not compute AFFO in the same manner as we do, and may use different terminology, our computation of AFFO may not be comparable to AFFO reported by other REITs or real estate companies. However, the Company believes that to further understand the performance of its stores, AFFO should be considered along with the net income and cash flows reported in accordance with GAAP and as presented in the Company's financial statements.

We believe net operating income or "NOI" is a meaningful measure of operating performance because we utilize NOI in making decisions with respect to, among other things, capital allocations, determining current store values, evaluating store performance, and in comparing period-to-period and market-to-market store operating results. In addition, we believe the investment community utilizes NOI in determining operating performance and real estate values and does not consider depreciation expense because it is based upon historical cost. NOI is defined as net store earnings before general and administrative expenses, interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization.

NOI is not a substitute for net income, net operating cash flow, or other related GAAP financial measures, in evaluating our operating results.

Same-Store Self Storage Operations Definition

We consider our same-store portfolio to consist of only those stores owned and operated on a stabilized basis at the beginning and at the end of the applicable periods presented. We consider a store to be stabilized once it has achieved an occupancy rate that we believe, based on our assessment of market-specific data, is representative of similar self storage assets in the applicable market for a full year measured as of the most recent January 1 and has not been significantly damaged by natural disaster or undergone significant renovation or expansion. We believe that same-store results are useful to investors in evaluating our performance because they provide information relating to changes in store-level operating performance without taking into account the effects of acquisitions, dispositions, or new ground-up developments. As of September 30, 2026, we owned twelve same-store properties and zero non-same-store properties. The Company believes that by providing same-store results from a stabilized pool of stores, with accompanying operating metrics including, but not limited to, variances in occupancy, rental revenue, operating expenses, and NOI, stockholders and potential investors are able to evaluate operating performance without the effects of non-stabilized occupancy levels, rent levels, expense levels, acquisitions, or completed developments. Same-store results should not be used as a basis for future same-store performance or for the performance of the Company's stores as a whole.

SHANGHAI, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- U Power Limited (Nasdaq: UCAR) (the "Company" or "U Power"), a provider of electric vehicle (EV) battery-swapping solutions based on its proprietary UOTTA™ technology, expanding into AI-integrated energy management for transportation systems and energy infrastructure, today announced its interim unaudited financial results for the six months ended June 30, 2026 ("H1 2026").[1]

H1 2026 Financial Snapshot

  • Total net revenues were RMB14.8 million (US$2.2 million), a decrease of 16.5% compared with RMB17.7 million in the six months ended June 30, 2025 ("H1 2025").
  • Combined net revenues from battery-swapping services, including two-wheeled vehicle battery-swapping services, increased 30.2% to RMB1.3 million (US$0.2 million), compared with RMB1.0 million in H1 2025.
  • Gross profit was RMB3.6 million (US$0.5 million), compared with RMB8.4 million in H1 2025. Gross margin was 24.5%.
  • Net loss was RMB97.6 million (US$14.4 million), compared with RMB27.4 million in H1 2025.
  • Cash and cash equivalents were RMB54.9 million (US$8.1 million) as of June 30, 2026, compared with RMB22.0 million as of December 31, 2025. Working capital was RMB123.3 million (US$18.2 million), compared with RMB65.5 million as of December 31, 2025.

Mr. Jia Li, CEO and Chairman of the Board of Directors of U Power, commented, "In the first half of 2026, we moved our two key battery-swapping projects from planning into execution. In Thailand, our first 30 battery-swapping heavy-duty trucks completed production and testing. In Hong Kong SAR, we commenced foundation works for our first MAXUS MIFA 7 battery-swapping taxi station. Subsequently, in August 2026, the first batch of these vehicles received type approval from the Transport Department, clearing them for sale in Hong Kong SAR.

"Total net revenues declined 16.5% year over year to RMB14.8 million, primarily due to the absence of sourcing services revenue, compared with RMB2.8 million in the first half of 2025, as the Thailand trucks we procured were not delivered to customers until July; and, to a lesser extent, a 3.1% decrease in revenue from sales of battery-swapping stations to RMB13.5 million. Revenue from battery-swapping services increased 30.2% year over year to RMB1.3 million as our two-wheeled vehicle battery-swapping business continued to scale.

"We received RMB207.2 million from the issuance of ordinary shares in the first half and ended the period with cash and cash equivalents of RMB54.9 million and working capital of RMB123.3 million. Our net loss primarily reflected expenses related to our overseas expansion and evaluation of potential investment targets, as well as a provision for expected credit losses and higher interest expenses.

"Our focus for the second half of the year is on converting our project pipeline into deliveries and recurring revenue, including our battery-swapping heavy-duty truck project in Thailand and our battery-swapping taxi project in Hong Kong SAR. Beyond mobility, we are developing AI-driven energy management solutions for intelligent data centers through our joint venture, which we believe can open a new avenue of growth by leveraging our expertise in energy infrastructure. We remain focused on disciplined execution as we work to build U Power into a diversified sustainable mobility and energy solutions provider and create long-term value for our shareholders."

[1] All amounts presented in U.S. dollars (US$) in this news release are based on a conversion rate of RMB6.7851 to US$1.00 for the reporting period ended June 30, 2026 and are provided solely for the convenience of the reader.

H1 2026 Financial Review

Total net revenues were RMB14.8 million (US$2.2 million), a decrease of 16.5% compared with RMB17.7 million in H1 2025, primarily due to the absence of sourcing services revenue, which was RMB2.8 million in H1 2025 and accounted for 15.9% of total net revenues in H1 2025, and, to a lesser extent, lower revenue from sales of battery-swapping stations. No sourcing services revenue was recorded in H1 2026 because the vehicles the Company procured during the period had not yet been sold as of June 30, 2026.

  • Net revenues from sales of battery-swapping stations were RMB13.5 million (US$2.0 million), a decrease of 3.1% compared with RMB13.9 million in H1 2025, and accounted for 91.0% of total net revenues.
  • Combined net revenues from battery-swapping services, including two-wheeled vehicle battery-swapping services, were RMB1.3 million (US$0.2 million), an increase of 30.2% compared with RMB1.0 million in H1 2025, and accounted for 9.0% of total net revenues. Revenues from two-wheeled vehicle battery-swapping services increased to RMB1.286 million from RMB0.675 million in H1 2025, partially offset by a decrease in revenues from other battery-swapping services to RMB0.039 million from RMB0.343 million in H1 2025.

Gross profit was RMB3.6 million (US$0.5 million), a decrease of 56.8% from RMB8.4 million in H1 2025, primarily due to lower gross profit from product sales, which fell to RMB4.2 million from RMB7.6 million in H1 2025. The decline primarily reflected the absence of sales of high-gross-margin battery-swapping stations by U SWAP, the Company's subsidiary in Thailand, which had occurred in H1 2025, as well as the sale of three additional battery-swapping stations with lower gross margins in H1 2026. Gross margin was 24.5%, compared with 47.3% in H1 2025, primarily due to the aforementioned factors along with higher per-unit procurement costs for the stations sold.

Total operating expenses were RMB83.8 million (US$12.3 million), an increase of 224.1% from RMB25.9 million in H1 2025, primarily reflecting higher general and administrative expenses and a provision for expected credit losses of RMB15.2 million (US$2.2 million), compared with a reversal of RMB3.9 million in H1 2025.

  • General and administrative expenses were RMB64.2 million (US$9.5 million), an increase of 161.5% from RMB24.6 million in H1 2025, primarily due to expenditures of approximately RMB11.7 million in identifying potential investment targets, approximately RMB11.2 million of consulting and other fees related to the localization of the Company's business in Thailand, approximately RMB5.1 million of operating and maintenance costs attributable to the Company's new business, and operating and maintenance costs incurred by newly added subsidiaries.
  • Research and development expenses were RMB3.3 million (US$0.5 million), a decrease of 4.4% from RMB3.4 million in H1 2025.
  • Sales and marketing expenses were RMB1.1 million (US$0.2 million), a decrease of 39.5% from RMB1.8 million in H1 2025, primarily attributable to reduced overseas business activities.

Interest income was RMB1.4 million (US$0.2 million), compared with RMB0.02 million in H1 2025, primarily due to higher interest income from third-party loans. Interest expenses were RMB9.0 million (US$1.3 million), compared with RMB0.2 million in H1 2025, primarily due to increases in loan interest and bank charges.

Net loss was RMB97.6 million (US$14.4 million), compared with a net loss of RMB27.4 million in H1 2025, primarily attributable to expenses related to overseas expansion and evaluation of potential investment targets, as well as a provision for expected credit losses and higher interest expenses. Net loss attributable to the Company's shareholders was RMB75.5 million (US$11.1 million), compared with RMB22.0 million in H1 2025.

Basic and diluted losses per ordinary share were RMB150.11 (US$22.13), compared with RMB1,157.27 in H1 2025, with weighted average ordinary shares outstanding of 502,968 and 19,010, respectively; per-share amounts for both periods have been retrospectively restated for the April 2026 share consolidation (1-for-10, effective April 1, 2026) and the September 2026 share consolidation (1-for-20, effective September 9, 2026).

Cash and cash equivalents were RMB54.9 million (US$8.1 million) as of June 30, 2026, compared with RMB22.0 million as of December 31, 2025, and working capital was RMB123.3 million (US$18.2 million), compared with RMB65.5 million. Total assets were RMB501.6 million (US$73.9 million), total liabilities were RMB104.8 million (US$15.4 million), and total shareholders' equity attributable to the Company's shareholders was RMB401.2 million (US$59.1 million), compared with RMB378.8 million, RMB84.2 million and RMB271.0 million, respectively, as of December 31, 2025.

Year-to-Date 2026 Operational Milestones

  • Thailand: Completed comprehensive operational testing and full-stack integration of the battery-swapping system on heavy-duty truck prototypes and completed production of the first batch of 30 trucks for Whale Logistics (Thailand) Co., Ltd., under a strategic partnership signed in December 2025 for the deployment of up to 1,000 battery-swapping electric truck tractors. The first batch arrived in Thailand in June 2026 and was delivered in July 2026. Construction of the first supporting battery-swapping station is under way, and the Company expects to complete its delivery in the second half of 2026.
  • Hong Kong SAR: In the first half of 2026, the Company commenced foundation works for the first MAXUS MIFA 7 battery-swapping taxi station at Container Terminal 9, Tsing Yi. The first batch of these vehicles to arrive in Hong Kong SAR received type approval from the Transport Department in August, clearing them for sale in Hong Kong SAR. The Company has been promoting the MIFA 7 battery-swapping taxi and the related battery-swapping operating model to taxi operators in Hong Kong SAR, and has received positive feedback from the industry. The Company expects to commence trial operation of battery-swapping services in Hong Kong SAR and start delivering battery-swap MIFA 7 vehicles to taxi companies by the end of 2026.
  • AI-driven intelligent data center (IDC) energy solutions: In April 2026, formed a joint venture with Guofu Hydrogen Energy (Hong Kong) Development Co., Limited (HKSE: 2582) and Cloud Digital Chain Limited to provide AI-driven energy management for IDCs, marking U Power's strategic expansion into the energy management solutions sector. In May 2026, the joint venture entered into an agreement with CEWA Group and Jiangsu Guofu Hydrogen Energy Equipment Co., Ltd. to develop an integrated energy solution for a planned 100MW data center in Rayong, Thailand, beginning with a 3MW pilot project.
  • Private placement: In August 2026, after the end of the reporting period, the Company completed a US$16 million private placement of 9,756,100 Class A ordinary shares to four existing shareholders at US$1.64 per share, equivalent to approximately 487,805 Class A ordinary shares at approximately US$32.80 per share after giving effect to the September 2026 share consolidation.

About U Power Limited

U Power is a provider of electric vehicle (EV) battery-swapping solutions based on its proprietary UOTTA™ technology, expanding into AI-integrated energy management for transportation systems and energy infrastructure. The Company has built a scalable network supporting commercial EV operations across multiple international markets.

U Power is now evolving beyond battery-swapping into an AI-driven, multi-energy ecosystem spanning EV infrastructure, smart energy management, and hydrogen power generation. Through a joint venture with a hydrogen technology company, the Company is developing integrated hydrogen-electric solutions for an Artificial Intelligence Data Center (AIDC) and EV charging and battery-swapping infrastructure, providing power support for electric mobility and the global AIDC industry.

For more information, please visit the Company's website: https://www.upower-limited.com/.

CAMDEN, N.J. and BRYN MAWR, Pa. , Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- American Water Works Company, Inc. (NYSE: AWK) ("American Water") and Essential Utilities, Inc. (NYSE: WTRG) ("Essential Utilities") today announced that the Illinois Commerce Commission issued an order approving the companies' proposed merger, marking the fourth favorable regulatory action toward completion of the transaction.

The companies previously received approval of the merger from the following regulatory commissions:

  • Virginia State Corporation Commission on June 22, 2026;
  • Public Utilities Commission of Ohio on May 13, 2026; and
  • Kentucky Public Service Commission on April 21, 2026.

Providing further momentum, settlement agreements in the merger approval proceedings have been reached in Pennsylvania, North Carolina, Texas, and New Jersey. Each agreement remains subject to review and approval by the applicable public utility commission.

Additionally, the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act expired on August 14, 2026, and shareholders of both companies overwhelmingly approved the transaction earlier this year.

The all-stock merger, announced October 27, 2025, will create a combined company serving more than 4.7 million water and wastewater customer connections and more than 740,000 natural gas customer connections. The combined company will operate under the American Water name and be headquartered in Camden, New Jersey.

The merger is expected to close by the end of the first quarter of 2027, but remains subject to customary closing conditions, including, among others, required regulatory approvals, including approval from the remaining applicable public utility commissions.

For additional details regarding the transaction, please visit americanwateressentialutilitiesmerger.com.

About American Water
American Water (NYSE: AWK) is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States. With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 19 military installations. American Water's approximately 7,000 talented professionals leverage their significant expertise and the company's national size and scale to achieve excellent outcomes for the benefit of customers, employees, investors and other stakeholders. For more information, visit amwater.com and join American Water on LinkedIn, Facebook, X and Instagram.

About Essential Utilities
Essential Utilities, Inc. (NYSE: WTRG) delivers safe, clean, reliable services that improve quality of life for individuals, families, and entire communities. With a focus on water, wastewater, and natural gas, Essential is committed to sustainable growth, operational excellence, a superior customer experience, and premier employer status. We are advocates for the communities we serve and are dedicated stewards of natural lands, protecting thousands of acres of forests and other habitats throughout our footprint.  Operating as the Aqua and Peoples brands, Essential serves approximately 5.5 million people across nine states. Essential is one of the most significant publicly traded water, wastewater service and natural gas providers in the U.S. Learn more at www.essential.co.

AUSTIN, Texas, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kestrel Group Ltd (NASDAQ: KG) ("Kestrel" or the "Company") a leading specialty insurance platform that provides fronting services to program managers, reinsurers, and reinsurance brokers, today reported its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Key Highlights – Third Quarter 2026 Financials

  • Program Services fee income of $2.9 million, up 203% year over year with a 71% margin on fee revenue
  • Program Services fee revenue of $4.1 million, up 151% year over year
  • Premium produced(1) by Program Services clients was $121.2 million, up 132% year over year
  • Total revenues were $4.8 million
  • Net premiums earned were $1.9 million
  • As of September 30, 2026, the Company's book value per common share(2) was $12.44
  • Net loss was $16.4 million, or a loss of $2.09 per share

Commenting on the results, Kestrel's Chief Executive Officer, Luke Ledbetter, stated, "Our Program Services segment continues to demonstrate strong sequential growth, with fee income, fee revenue and premium produced up once again, both from the second quarter of 2026 and year-over-year. This marks improvement in each quarter of 2026, driven by solid execution and our expanding pipeline of opportunity, and we are encouraged by the positive momentum within this segment. As we focus on the areas of our business with the greatest potential return for shareholders, we remain committed to optimizing our cost structure. Toward that end, we are pursuing broad-based expense reduction initiatives which have made significant progress during the third quarter, and we are targeting approximately $5 million in run-rate expense savings over the next year."

Program Services Segment

The Program Services segment provides fronting services to general agents and insurance carriers to leverage Kestrel's trusted reputation to provide access to the U.S. property and casualty insurance market and insurance paper rated "A-" (Excellent) by A.M. Best and expansive licenses in exchange for fees. Kestrel issues the policy through exclusive use of four insurance carriers, and those carriers presently retain and reinsure the risk. The Company continues to actively pursue reinsurance mechanisms with its existing partners that would selectively deploy the Company's underwriting capacity that it believes could facilitate and accelerate both its fee and premium revenue growth.

Program Services' fee income for the third quarter of 2026 was $2.9 million, up 203% compared to the same quarter in 2025. Total fee revenues for the quarter were $4.1 million, up 151% from the third quarter of 2025, driven by growth in both existing and new client accounts. Premium produced(1) by client programs totaled $121.2 million for the quarter, up 132% year over year.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Program Services' fee income was $6.9 million, compared to $1.0 million for the same period in 2025. Total fee revenues for the period were $10.9 million, compared to $3.0 million in 2025, reflecting higher premium produced by both new and existing client programs. Premium produced(1) for the nine months totaled $325.0 million, up 244% from the prior-year period.

Legacy Reinsurance Segment

The Legacy Reinsurance segment consists of the AmTrust Reinsurance and Diversified Reinsurance segments previously reported by Maiden Holdings, Ltd. ("Maiden") prior to the Combination with Kestrel. The AmTrust portion of this segment includes all business ceded to Maiden Reinsurance Ltd. by AmTrust. The Diversified portion of this segment consists of a run-off portfolio of predominantly third-party property and casualty reinsurance business focusing on regional and specialty property and casualty insurance companies located primarily in Europe, as well as business produced by Maiden LF and Maiden GF along with transactions entered into by Genesis Legacy Solutions.

During the third quarter of 2026, the Legacy Reinsurance segment reported an underwriting loss of $6.4 million, consisting of $0.1 million of underwriting income from the AmTrust business and a $6.5 million underwriting loss from the Diversified business.

The AmTrust business reported a current accident year underwriting loss of $1.4 million as the run-off of certain remaining multiple-year policies continues. This was offset by net favorable prior period development ("PPD") of $1.4 million, primarily experienced from movement not subject to the LPT/ADC Agreement including favorable movement in Workers' Compensation and Program exposure partially offset by adverse development in Specialty Risk lines of business in the AmTrust Quota Share. PPD was also affected by foreign currency movements on loss reserves denominated in non-USD currencies, which had an adverse impact of $1.3 million. Excluding foreign exchange, PPD for the AmTrust business was favorable by $2.7 million.

The Diversified business' results largely reflect the ongoing run-off of the Company's international operations. Its $6.5 million underwriting loss included $3.1 million of loss development on the German Auto quota share in the IIS unit, after the cedant triggered contractual inflation-related adjustments that increased the Company's exposure, and a $2.4 million settlement of a Genesis Legacy Solutions claim.

Investment Activities and Other Gains

The Company reported a net loss from investment activities of $1.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, consisting of net investment income of $2.3 million, offset by net realized and unrealized investment losses of $3.6 million, which reflected fair value adjustments on certain of the Company's alternative and real estate assets.

The Company also recognized foreign exchange and other gains of $0.7 million for the quarter, primarily consisting of $0.5 million of net foreign exchange gains and a $0.1 million gain from the revaluation of a contingent receivable in the insurance distribution industry. The foreign exchange gains resulted from the appreciation of the U.S. dollar on the remeasurement of net loss reserves and insurance-related liabilities denominated in non-USD currencies.

General and Administrative Expenses

Total general and administrative expenses were $11.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $11.8 million for the third quarter of 2025. Segment G&A expenses fell to $3.4 million from $4.4 million. Corporate G&A expenses rose to $8.0 million from $7.4 million. The increase was driven mainly by higher share-based compensation of $1.6 million (versus $0.2 million) and by higher recurring compensation, legal and professional fees. Lower non-recurring expenses of $0.5 million (versus $2.3 million) partly offset these increases.

Segment G&A expenses for the quarter included $0.3 million in fair value adjustments recognized in connection with the Company's May 27, 2025 combination with Maiden. Non-recurring segment G&A expense includes costs for the GLS arbitration while non-recurring corporate G&A expenses include costs for the restructuring and severance (including $0.5 million of employee separation charges incurred in the quarter) and the Combination. These costs are excluded from the Company's non-GAAP operating loss. See "Non-GAAP Financial Measures."

The Company is carrying out broad-based initiatives to reduce its operating cost structure. It expects these actions to produce annualized run-rate savings of approximately $5 million, with the full run-rate expected within the next twelve months. Actions taken to date include:

  • significantly reducing costs associated with a broad range of professional and advisory services;
  • outsourcing a substantial portion of the Company's information technology infrastructure and support functions, completed early in the fourth quarter of 2026; and
  • streamlining certain internal functions, including related headcount reductions and the selective use of third-party service providers.

The Company continues to evaluate and implement a range of additional measures and may incur additional employee separation and other non-recurring charges as these initiatives are completed.

Balance Sheet

Total assets were $879.6 million at September 30, 2026, and shareholders' equity was $97.8 million.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company has available net operating loss ("NOL") carryforwards of $477.8 million for income tax purposes. Approximately $390.2 million of NOL carryforwards expire in various years beginning in 2029. As of September 30, 2026, approximately $87.6 million or 18.3% of the Company's NOL carryforwards have no expiry date under the relevant U.S. tax law.

Book value per common share is calculated using shareholders' equity divided by the number of common shares outstanding excluding unvested restricted and performance shares. Management uses growth in this metric as a prime measure of the value we are generating for our common shareholders, because management believes that growth in this metric ultimately results in growth in the Company's common share price. This metric is impacted by the Company's net income and external factors, such as interest rates, which can drive changes in unrealized gains or losses on our investment portfolio as well as share repurchases.

This measure is also a useful tool to measure the profitability of the Company separately from the investment results and is also a widely used performance indicator in the insurance industry.

Non-GAAP operating earnings (loss) and non-GAAP basic and diluted operating earnings (loss) per common share are non-GAAP financial measures defined by the Company as net income (loss) excluding realized investment gains and losses, foreign exchange and other gains and losses, interest in income (loss) of equity method investment, and amortization of intangible assets and should not be considered as an alternative to net income (loss). It also excludes on a non-recurring basis: (1) litigation costs related to the GLS Arbitration; (2) restructuring and severance costs; and (3) costs incurred due to the Combination; (4) Change in fair value of earn out consideration; and (5) Change in bargain purchase gain. Management also believes that these measures generally follow industry practice therefore allowing the users of financial information to compare the Company's performance with its industry peer group, and that the equity analysts and certain rating agencies which follow the Company, and the insurance industry as a whole, generally exclude these items from their analyses for the same reasons. Non-GAAP operating earnings should not be viewed as a substitute for U.S. GAAP net income.



(6)

Non-GAAP operating return on average shareholders' equity is a non-GAAP financial measure. Management uses non-GAAP operating return on average shareholders' equity as a measure of profitability that focuses on the return to common shareholders. It is calculated using non-GAAP operating earnings divided by average shareholders' equity.



(7)

Kyoto event generates approximately US$1.3 million in service revenue for FiEE, highlighting opportunities in next-generation art discovery and collector engagement

OSAKA, Japan, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FiEE, Inc. (NASDAQ: FIEE) ("FiEE" or the "Company"), a technology company integrating Internet of Things ("IoT"), connectivity, and artificial intelligence ("AI") to redefine brand management solutions, today announced the successful completion of its international art exhibition and accompanying auction in Kyoto, Japan. The event marks a milestone in FiEE's evolution toward an online-to-offline ("O2O") ecosystem integrating art and technology ("ArtTech"), connecting artists and global collectors through digital engagement, physical experiences, and commercial transactions.

Organized by the Company's subsidiary, FiEE Channel Limited, in partnership with the Museum of Kyoto, Harmony of Ink: FAx26 Kyoto International Contemporary Art Exchange Exhibition took place from October 23 to 25, 2026. The accompanying auction, held on October 23, 2026, attracted nearly 400 participants online and in person, resulting in an aggregate artwork transaction value of approximately US$2.9 million. The aggregate transaction value represents artwork sales, not the Company's revenue. FiEE generated approximately US$1.3 million in service revenue from the auction, highlighting the commercial potential of its O2O business model. Building on this success, FiEE plans to organize regular art appreciation and networking events to deepen collector engagement and create additional revenue opportunities.

Discovering hidden gems: Engaging the next generation of collectors

FiEE sees opportunities to engage younger collectors, including millennials (Generation Y) and members of Generation Z, who seek originality, cultural identity, and emerging artistic talent beyond established names.

Leveraging its network of key opinion leaders ("KOLs"), digital content capabilities, and curated exhibitions, FiEE aims to connect artists with collectors seeking distinctive artworks and hidden gems. By combining online discovery with physical experiences, the Company seeks to make art more accessible while expanding international exposure for artists.

Beyond transactions: Art advisory as a service

FiEE believes artwork acquisition should mark the beginning of a lasting collector relationship. The Company sees opportunities to develop art advisory services that would offer personalized artwork recommendations, artist introductions, acquisition assistance, collection development, and post-transaction support.

Complementary offerings, including artwork safekeeping, promotional services, and exhibition opportunities, could further strengthen collector relationships. By extending engagement beyond individual purchases, FiEE aims to encourage repeat transactions and generate advisory fees and recurring service revenue, supporting a more diversified business model.

Connecting online discovery with offline experiences

FiEE's O2O strategy integrates digital engagement with physical cultural experiences, creating a connected journey from artwork discovery to acquisition. The Company's software-as-a-service ("SaaS") solutions support this strategy. The FiEE Channel App supports content creation, social media amplification, and audience acquisition, while the Fontree App enables online participation in curated art sales and facilitates transactions. Physical exhibitions and private events are intended to complement these platforms, allowing collectors to experience artworks firsthand and build relationships with artists.

Together, these channels create opportunities for continued engagement, repeat participation, and additional value-added services.

Rafael Li, Chief Executive Officer and President of FiEE, commented, "The success of our Kyoto art exhibition and accompanying auction highlights FiEE's ability to translate digital engagement into meaningful commercial transactions while establishing a foundation for a broader ArtTech ecosystem. We see exciting opportunities among younger collectors seeking hidden gems and emerging talent. By seeking to combine personalized art advisory, curated experiences, and a global collector network, we aim to make art discovery more accessible and rewarding.

"Our vision extends beyond individual transactions. We aim to connect online discovery with offline experiences and build lasting relationships between artists and collectors, with the goal of unlocking new revenue opportunities and creating long-term value for our stockholders."

About FiEE, Inc.

FiEE, Inc. (NASDAQ: FIEE), formerly Minim, Inc., was founded in 1977. It has a historical track record of delivering a comprehensive WiFi/SaaS platform in the market. After years of development, it made the strategic decision to transition to a Software First Model in 2024 to expand its technology portfolio and revenue streams. In 2025, FiEE, Inc. rebranded itself as a technology company leveraging its expertise in IoT, connectivity, and AI to explore new business prospects and extend its global footprint.

FiEE, Inc.'s services are structured into four key categories: Cloud-Managed Connectivity (WiFi) Platform, IoT Hardware Sales & Licensing, SaaS Solutions, and Professional To-C and To-B Services & Support. Notably, FiEE, Inc. has introduced its innovative SaaS solutions, which integrate its AI and data analytics capabilities into content creation and brand management. This initiative has nurtured a robust pool of KOLs on major social media platforms worldwide, helping them develop, manage, and optimize their digital presence. FiEE, Inc.'s services include customized graphics and posts, short videos, and editorial calendars tailored to align with brand objectives.

SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif., Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Nkarta, Inc. (Nasdaq: NKTX), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing engineered natural killer (NK) cell therapies to treat autoimmune diseases, today announced that it will host a webcast on Monday, November 9, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. ET, to review initial clinical data from its Ntrust program evaluating NKX019 in myositis and systemic sclerosis being presented at the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Convergence 2026 in Orlando.

A replay will be archived on the Investors section of Nkarta’s website, www.nkartatx.com.

About the Ntrust℠ Clinical Trials in Autoimmune Disease
Ntrust-1 (NCT06557265) and Ntrust-2 (NCT06733935) are multi-center, open-label, dose-escalation clinical trials in patients with autoimmune disease receiving lymphodepletion followed by CD19-targeted CAR-NK cell therapy. Both trials assess the safety of NKX019 in people living with autoimmune diseases as well as its potential to achieve durable remission via a “reset” of the immune system through the elimination of pathogenic B cells.  

The Ntrust trials are enrolling up to 12 patients per dose level per disease indication, with leading indications in myositis and systemic sclerosis, as well as ANCA-associated vasculitis, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus nephritis, and primary membranous nephropathy. Additional patients may be enrolled if needed to refine patient populations for further study.

In both studies, patients receive a three-dose cycle of NKX019 following lymphodepletion with fludarabine and cyclophosphamide or cyclophosphamide alone, if they have significant cytopenia at baseline. This approach is designed to evaluate the single-agent activity of NKX019 and facilitate a more rapid path to regulatory approval. Patients in both trials may also receive additional cycles, if needed, to restore response or enable a deeper response.
   
About NKX019
NKX019 is an allogeneic, cryopreserved, off-the-shelf immunotherapy candidate that uses natural killer (NK) cells derived from the peripheral blood of healthy adult donors. It is engineered with a humanized CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) for enhanced cell targeting and a proprietary, membrane-bound form of interleukin-15 (IL-15) for greater persistence and activity without exogenous cytokine support. CD19 is a biomarker for normal B cells as well as those implicated in autoimmune disease. Nkarta is evaluating NKX019 in multiple autoimmune conditions.

About Nkarta
Nkarta is a clinical-stage biotechnology company advancing the development of allogeneic, off-the-shelf natural killer (NK) cell therapies for people living with autoimmune diseases. By harnessing the power of the innate immune system to eliminate pathogenic B cells driving the autoimmune response, Nkarta is advancing novel cell therapies engineered for deep therapeutic impact. The on-demand availability and outpatient dosing of our CAR-NK cells enable a broad population of patients with different autoimmune conditions to conveniently access NK cell therapy in community health settings. Key Terms

fcrnmedical
The neonatal Fc receptor (FCRN or FcRn) is a protein that controls how long antibodies and the blood protein albumin stay in circulation by protecting them from being broken down. For investors, therapies that block or harness FcRn can change a drug’s dosing, effectiveness and market appeal—either by lengthening beneficial antibodies for longer-lasting treatments or by reducing harmful antibodies in autoimmune disease—so progress in FcRn-targeted programs can materially affect a biotech’s commercial value.
igf-1rmedical
A protein on the surface of cells that acts like an antenna for a growth signal called insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1); when IGF-1 binds this receptor, it tells cells to grow and survive. Investors care because many experimental drugs aim to block or modulate this receptor to treat cancers and other diseases, so clinical trial results, regulatory decisions, or safety findings related to IGF-1R can strongly influence a biotech company’s value and risk profile.
